first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) map directly onto prior validated interventions (memory_31, memory_86) showing durable activation/completion lifts from onboarding simplification. I verify these two since they're the strongest causal candidates for the actual metrics that moved, and stacking two consistent inherited results increases confidence they generalize. I deliberately do not spend verification budget or this week's single experiment slot on promotional_pricing: matching a competitor's aggressive entry pricing is tempting reactively, but memory_73's evidence is about proactive targeted pricing in a different competitive context, and reflexively price-matching risks acquiring lower-quality, price-sensitive accounts that erode sustainable qualified revenue even if memory_73 were re-verified as accurate. Given only one experiment slot and no rollover, and given two metrics simultaneously declining (suggesting a possible structural onboarding issue rather than a one-off), I favor a small guarded test of onboarding simplification rather than broad rollout, preserving the option to reassess if this quarter's decline has a different root cause than prior quarters. Enterprise and referral paths are unaffected by the current metric drops and are deprioritized this cycle.
